The newly focused parent company must now be evaluated based on its standalone operating performance and recurring economics rather than historical consolidated results [D01].

final.memo:
Baxter International stands at a critical juncture following the July 1, 2015 separation of its bioscience operation [D01]. The market currently views the company as a burdened entity, but we see potential for significant value creation if the newly focused medical-products business can eliminate legacy overhead and align its margins with premier peers like Becton Dickinson and Danaher [D01; D03; D06].

At present, the investment case remains speculative due to the lack of a reconciled standalone balance sheet and clarity on normalized post-spin earnings power [D04]. We lack the necessary financial data to confirm a valuation floor or the 3:1 risk/reward skew required for a core position [D04].

Our plan, should we engage, would be to demand a rigorous cost-structure optimization and a transparent capital allocation policy [D01; D03]. We expect the CEO and Board to provide a concrete roadmap for margin convergence within the next two quarters [D03; D05].

Given the uncertainty surrounding the post-spin execution and the lack of differentiated insight into the standalone cost structure, we are passing on the opportunity at this time [D05; D07]. We will monitor the situation and wait for management to demonstrate operational progress before committing capital.
